content.title: Engaging students to enhance learning
content.summary: The Network of Teaching and Learning explores ways to engage students in the classroom.

content.text: 'Phones and other mobile devices distract students during lessons' is a statement commonly made by teachers. But the bigger question is whether there are any opportunities to use these devices to support learning?

The Network of Teaching and Learning (TL_net) believes there is and its conviction is backed up by research that has repeatedly shown that these devices - when used correctly - can increase student engagement and deepen learning in today's world.

To demonstrate how mobile devices can facilitate active learning, TL_net is set to host the second session of its Flipped Learning series on July 14 and July 19. Flipped Learning reverses when and where content review, the 'real' learning, happens. Class time is no longer for lectures but for group-based assignments or problem solving activities. Students having reviewed content out-of-class, come prepared for its application in class.

In TL_net's first session in March, instructors Edward Ombajo and Louisa Lambregts showed how tools such as the web-based Kahoot application can be used to confirm understanding of content. Smartphones, tablets and laptops, devices that students have with them in class, can then be used for learning.

Kahoot and similar web-based applications can help teachers quickly gauge the class's grasp of concepts and fluidly adjust to include a review of what is not understood. They also provide an alternative form of classroom learning engagement through which all students - not just those who put up their hands - can actively participate.

Speaking about the session, Edward Ombajo said: "Our goal is to help teachers feel confident and competent in the use of digital teaching tools. So far we've introduced faculty to a new approach and in the future we hope to introduce guidelines on teaching with technology at AKU. We are eager to explore how integrating technology can help support active, engaged learning approaches."

"We had over 90 students and faculty across all of AKU's campuses attend our first meeting and our next session will focus on giving faculty a chance to experience 'flipped' learning first-hand. Participants will learn how to set-up and implement Kahoot and Padlet to support a flipped lesson."
The July workshop will be led by Edward Misava, Raheel Lakhani and Louisa Lambregts supported by face-to-face facilitators at each location in Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Pakistan and the UK.
